criterion_notes.c1: Yes. The document addresses household and community deficits in basic sanitation and drinking-water supply (water network coverage, sewerage, latrines, and safe water supply) in the district/settlement of Secocha, Camaná province, Arequipa region, Peru.
criterion_notes.c2: No under both the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading and the plain wording of Criterion 2. Narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Fails because the work does not examine any rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, enforcement/disconnection, or utility regulatory structure); instead, it proposes generic community public-health interventions (dry latrine installation, household water storage/chlorination, hygiene workshops, and community health monitoring) while citing weak local institutional management and low state investment only as unanalysed background. Plain wording: Also fails (and would still be excluded overall) because institutional coordination and municipal capacity are mentioned only as general background causes and proposed stakeholder roles in an action plan rather than an empirically analysed legal, administrative, or governance factor.
criterion_notes.c3: No. This is a postgraduate capstone action-plan proposal (Trabajo Académico: Plan de acción) with no primary empirical results reported and not a systematic synthesis. Although the abstract and Section 3.2 mention a mixed-methods diagnostic design with 120 households and include blank data-collection templates in Annexes 1–5, Table 3 describes the planned data analyses in the future tense (e.g., 'Se aplicarán métodos estadísticos descriptivos', 'Se empleará técnicas cualitativas'), Section 4.5 reports only projected targets ('Resultados Esperados'), and zero survey statistics, interview data, or systematic observación results appear anywhere in the text.
criterion_notes.c4: No. No measured empirical service-access outcome is reported; basic sanitation coverage and safe-water access appear only as planned diagnostic indicators (Table 3) and projected targets in Section 4.5 (80% expected coverage), while the primary health problem framed in the title is acute diarrheal infection (IDA) in children under five.
criterion_notes.c5: No. Because the document is a non-empirical action plan presenting future-tense analysis methods, blank instruments (Annexes 1–5), and projected outcomes rather than executed empirical analysis, an empirical study design, measured exposure, and measured outcome cannot be identified.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes (via Criterion 10). The full text is in Spanish (with an English Summary on PDF page 14); direct comprehension and translation from the readable Spanish full text are fully feasible for screening assessment.

evidence_quotes.quote: La investigación analiza la crisis de acceso a servicios básicos de saneamiento en el distrito de Secocha, provincia de Camaná, región Arequipa (Perú), y su relación con la alta incidencia de infecciones diarreicas agudas (IDA) en niños menores de cinco años.

Elaborar un plan de acción para la implementación de estrategias ante el desabastecimiento del sistema de saneamiento básico como factor contribuyente a las infecciones diarreicas agudas en niños menores de 5 años en Secocha, 2025.
Planteamiento de soluciones sostenibles, incluyendo la instalación de baños secos, mecanismos para el almacenamiento de agua y talleres de educación sanitaria
Se empleará técnicas cualitativas para identificar patrones recurrentes en los datos obtenidos de entrevistas.
Se espera que el 80% de los hogares en situación vulnerable accedan a servicios básicos de saneamiento adecuados.

raw_response.exposure: Deficit in basic sanitation and water supply infrastructure; proposed community sanitation and hygiene education action plan (dry latrines, safe water storage, handwashing workshops)
raw_response.outcome: Projected reduction in acute diarrheal infections (IDA) in children under 5 years (40% target) and projected household basic sanitation coverage (80% target); no empirical outcomes reported
raw_response.population_and_sample: Target community of Secocha, Camaná province, Arequipa, Peru (families with children under 5 years; 120 households proposed for diagnostic sampling, along with health personnel, local authorities, and community leaders, with no empirical sample data reported)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence), and also fails Criterion 2 and Criterion 4. The retrieved 65-page Spanish postgraduate Trabajo Académico is a public-health action-plan proposal ('Plan de acción') for Secocha, Peru, rather than a completed empirical study or systematic synthesis: its diagnostic analysis table is written in the future tense (Table 3), Annexes 1–5 contain only blank survey/interview/observation forms, Section 4.5 states projected 'Resultados Esperados', and zero primary quantitative or qualitative findings are reported. Moreover, it does not examine any legal, regulatory, or administrative rule-type mechanism governing water or sanitation access (focusing instead on basic sanitation infrastructure shortages, hygiene promotion workshops, and dry latrine installation to prevent pediatric diarrheal disease), so it is excluded under both the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading and the plain wording of Criterion 2.
raw_response.study_design: Non-empirical public-health action plan proposal (proposes a mixed-methods participatory situational diagnosis, but reports future-tense analysis plans, blank instruments, and projected targets with no primary empirical data)
